procedures.symptom: Unit completely dead — no fans, no compressor, no board lights, no thermostat display
safety: Prove the meter live-dead-live; a dead-reading panel may still be live on one leg (single-pole failure, blown fuse on one phase).
480/575 V: CAT III/IV meter and arc-rated PPE (NFPA 70E) for live checks at the disconnect and panel.
Lock out and tag before touching line-voltage terminals.

steps.step: Confirm the disconnect is on and the pull-out/fuse block is fully seated; read line-to-line voltage on the LINE side of the disconnect (all legs).
steps.expect: Nominal voltage on every leg pair (208-230/460/575 ±10 %).
steps.ifNot: Upstream: breaker in the building panel (reset fully OFF then ON), utility, a tripped main. If the breaker trips again immediately, do not keep resetting — find the fault.

steps.step: Read line-to-line on the LOAD side of the disconnect/fuses; read across each fuse.
steps.expect: Same voltage as the line side; ~0 V across each fuse.
steps.ifNot: Line voltage across a fuse = blown fuse (replace with the same type/size and find why); no load-side voltage with good fuses = open disconnect pole.

steps.step: Read voltage at the unit's terminal block / contactor line side, and check the unit's own branch protection (fuses, breakers inside the unit, blower door interlock switch).
steps.expect: Line voltage at the unit terminal block.
steps.ifNot: Burned lug, broken wire in the whip, open door switch — repair the connection.

steps.step: Read the control transformer: primary voltage at the tap in use, then secondary (24 VAC) at the transformer and at the board R–C.
steps.expect: Primary present; 24–28 VAC secondary; 24 V at R–C.
steps.ifNot: Primary present, no secondary = transformer open (check the wrong-tap/overload cause first); secondary present at the transformer but not at R–C = blown control fuse/board breaker (3 A) — find the 24 V short before replacing (see intermittent 24 V loss).

steps.step: If the control fuse is good and R–C reads 24 V but the board shows no LED/status: check the board's line-voltage supply (120/240 V L1–N or L1–L2 to the board), its own fuse, and the thermostat display (a dead stat with 24 V at the unit = stat wire or stat).
steps.expect: Board LED on; thermostat display on.
steps.ifNot: Board with power in and no life = board; stat dead with R–C present at the unit = open R/C wire to the stat or a dead stat.

steps.step: With power restored, verify the safeties and check why the failure happened (thermostat wire short, a grounded component, water intrusion in the disconnect, a compressor short that blew the fuses).
steps.expect: Unit responds to a call; no repeat fuse/breaker trips.
steps.ifNot: Go to 'breaker/fuse trips' if protection opens again.

commonCauses: Tripped breaker or blown fuse (often from a shorted compressor, condenser fan motor, or water in the disconnect)
Disconnect pull-out removed or a burned pole
Blown control (3 A) fuse from a shorted thermostat wire or 24 V coil
Failed control transformer (wrong tap, overload, secondary short)
Open blower door interlock, loose lug, rodent-chewed whip
Dead thermostat / BAS controller power supply

procedures.symptom: No cooling — indoor and/or condenser fans run but the compressor is off
safety: Contactor line side is live with the unit idle; keep fingers and probes clear of the line terminals.
Momentary diagnostic jumpers only — attended, seconds, removed before leaving. Never jumper the RDS/mitigation on A2L units.
Discharge capacitors before handling.

steps.step: Read any fault code on the board / thermostat / phase monitor / compressor protection module first (HPS, LPS, lockout, ASC delay, RDS mitigation, phase loss).
steps.expect: Code identifies the open safety or a delay in progress.
steps.ifNot: No code: continue tracing; note that a blinking 'delay' may just be the anti-short-cycle timer (wait 5 min).

steps.step: Verify the cooling call is arriving: Y1 (and Y2 if staged) to C at the unit terminal strip = 24 VAC with the stat/BAS calling.
steps.expect: 24 VAC on Y1–C.
steps.ifNot: No Y: thermostat/BAS (setpoint, mode, schedule, override, compressor lockout) or the stat wire — see 'call present but unit idle'.

steps.step: Trace the 24 V safety chain from Y toward the contactor coil: read across HPS, LPS/LOC, freeze stat, condensate switch, duct smoke, fire relay, phase monitor contact, ASC timer.
steps.expect: ~0 V across every device; 24 V arrives at the contactor coil.
steps.ifNot: 24 V across a device = it is open — diagnose that device (pressures with gauges for HPS/LPS, coil temp for freeze stat, phase monitor LED, timer).

steps.step: At the contactor: 24 V across the coil? Is the armature pulled in?
steps.expect: Coil energized and pulled in.
steps.ifNot: Coil voltage present, not pulled in = open coil or jammed armature (ohm the coil, power off); pulled in but no compressor = go on.

steps.step: Contactor pulled in: read line voltage on the LOAD side (T1–T2, T2–T3, T3–T1 for 3-ph; T1–T2 for 1-ph) and the drop across each pole.
steps.expect: Full voltage on all legs at the load side, < 0.5 V across each pole.
steps.ifNot: Missing leg = burned pole/blown fuse (single-phasing); replace the contactor / fuse.

steps.step: Voltage at the compressor terminals with 0 A: power off, cool-down consideration, then ohm the windings and megger to ground (see the compressor components).
steps.expect: Windings per pattern, > 100 MΩ.
steps.ifNot: Open overload hot → cool 1–2 h and retest; open winding/grounded → compressor.

steps.step: Compressor hums or trips: single-phase → run capacitor under load, start components; 3-phase → voltage imbalance, rotation, single-phasing. See the dedicated procedures.
steps.expect: Root cause found and corrected; compressor runs with amps ≤ RLA.
steps.ifNot: Escalate to refrigeration-side diagnosis (locked from slugging, high head).

commonCauses: Open safety in the Y chain (HPS after a dirty condenser or dead condenser fan; LPS/LOC from low charge)
Board lockout after repeated safety trips (needs a reset after the fix)
Contactor coil open or burned contacts
Compressor internal overload open (hot) — cool down and re-test
Anti-short-cycle or thermostat delay still timing
RDS mitigation active on A2L units (blower forced on, compressor locked out)
Phase monitor tripped (phase loss/reversal) on 3-phase units

procedures.symptom: Single-phase compressor hums / buzzes and won't start, then trips on overload
safety: Stand to the side of the compressor terminal cover when starting; a weakened terminal can vent (terminal venting hazard). Never start with the terminal cover off.
Discharge run and start capacitors through a bleed resistor before handling.
Do not keep hitting the compressor with LRA — each attempt heats the windings; limit attempts and let it cool.

steps.step: Confirm line voltage at the compressor while it tries to start (contactor closed): read at the contactor load side during the hum.
steps.expect: ≥ 90 % of nominal during the start attempt (e.g. ≥ 207 V on a 230 V unit).
steps.ifNot: Voltage sags badly = undersized wire, bad connection, utility; fix the supply first.

steps.step: Check the run capacitor under load (or bench) on the HERM section: µF = 2652 × A / V on the HERM lead.
steps.expect: Within ±6 % of rating; can not bulged/leaking.
steps.ifNot: Weak/open cap → replace with the same µF and equal-or-higher volts; retest the start.

steps.step: If a start capacitor/potential relay (or hard-start kit) is fitted: check the start cap (printed range, vent intact, bleed resistor) and the relay contacts 1–2 (closed at rest) and coil 2–5.
steps.expect: Start cap within −0/+20 %; relay contacts closed at rest, coil continuous.
steps.ifNot: Replace the failed start component (kit) with the correct rating for the compressor.

steps.step: Check the pressure differential: has the compressor been off long enough to equalize (3–5 min)? Is there a stuck TXV/check valve holding head pressure?
steps.expect: Suction and discharge nearly equal before the start.
steps.ifNot: Wait for equalization; if it never equalizes, diagnose the refrigerant side; a hard-start kit may be justified on a non-equalizing system.

steps.step: Power off, leads off: ohm C-S, C-R, S-R and megger to ground; consider the compressor temperature.
steps.expect: C-S + C-R ≈ S-R within 10 %, no 0 Ω, > 100 MΩ to ground.
steps.ifNot: Shorted/grounded winding → compressor. Open C-S/C-R with S-R intact → overload open, cool 1–2 h.

steps.step: All electrical checks pass and it still draws LRA and trips: a mechanically locked compressor (liquid slugging, oil loss, bearing seizure). Try a hard-start kit once as a diagnostic; if the compressor still will not start, condemn it.
steps.expect: Starts with the kit → compressor is tight but usable (investigate why: flood-back, crankcase heater, migration); still LRA → replace.
steps.ifNot: Before replacement: acid test the oil, check for flood-back causes (charge, TXV, airflow) so the new compressor survives.

commonCauses: Weak or open run capacitor (most common)
Failed start capacitor / potential relay on CSR compressors
Low line voltage or a bad connection at start
Starting against an unequalized head pressure (short cycle, stuck check valve)
Liquid refrigerant in the compressor (migration; failed crankcase heater)
Mechanically seized compressor (bearing, scroll set, oil loss)

procedures.symptom: Three-phase compressor won't start — hums, trips, or nothing
safety: 460/575 V: CAT III/IV meter and leads, arc-rated PPE per NFPA 70E for live measurements.
Never energize a compressor with the terminal cover removed; stand to the side.
Lock out and verify all three legs dead before ohming windings; never megger under vacuum or with a VFD connected.

steps.step: Read all three line-to-line voltages at the contactor line side with the unit idle and during the start attempt.
steps.expect: All three present and balanced within 2 % (NEMA MG-1); no leg collapses on start.
steps.ifNot: A missing/low leg = blown fuse, burned disconnect pole, utility phase loss — see 'phase loss / single-phasing'. Imbalance > 2 %: fix before running.

steps.step: Contactor pulled in? Read the drop across each pole under the start attempt and the load-side voltages T1–T2, T2–T3, T3–T1.
steps.expect: < 0.5 V across each pole; full voltage on all three load-side pairs.
steps.ifNot: One pole open/burned = single-phasing the compressor (loud hum, no start) — replace the contactor.

steps.step: Check the phase monitor / compressor protection module LED and the board code (phase loss, reversal, unbalance, high discharge temperature, CoreSense codes).
steps.expect: OK / no fault.
steps.ifNot: Correct the condition the monitor reports; a reversal after power work → swap two line leads at the unit line side.

steps.step: Clamp each leg during the start: LRA for > 2–3 s then trip = locked rotor or single-phased; 0 A on one leg = open leg/winding.
steps.expect: Brief inrush then amps settle near/below RLA.
steps.ifNot: Continue to winding checks.

steps.step: Power off, leads off: ohm T1–T2, T2–T3, T3–T1 and megger each to ground at 500 VDC.
steps.expect: Legs equal within ±5 %; > 100 MΩ.
steps.ifNot: All open on a hot shell = internal overload; cool 1–2 h. One leg open/shorted or < 1 MΩ → compressor.

steps.step: Scroll compressors that start but are loud with no pressure differential and low amps: reversed rotation — verify with a phase rotation meter and correct at the line side.
steps.expect: Correct rotation: pressures separate, normal sound, amps near RLA.
steps.ifNot: If rotation is correct and it still will not pump: failed scroll set / IPR open → compressor.

commonCauses: Single-phasing: blown fuse on one leg, burned contactor pole, open lug
Phase monitor or protection module lockout (phase loss/reversal/unbalance)
Voltage imbalance > 2 % overheating the motor
Internal overload open from a previous overheating event
Reversed rotation after utility/disconnect work
Open or grounded winding, mechanically seized compressor

procedures.symptom: Breaker trips or fuses blow (immediately or after running)
safety: A breaker that trips instantly indicates a short or ground fault — do not reset repeatedly; each reset is an arc event. Isolate the fault first.
Lock out before ohming or meggering; discharge capacitors; disconnect VFDs and electronic controls before meggering.
Replace fuses with the same class/size (time-delay, per nameplate MOP); never upsize.

steps.step: Establish the pattern: trips on the compressor start (instant), after minutes of running, or randomly; which protection opens (unit fuses, building breaker, control fuse).
steps.expect: Pattern points to short (instant), overload (delayed), or intermittent connection/water (random).
steps.ifNot: Ask the site for history; check the breaker itself (warm, worn, many resets).

steps.step: Power off, locked out: megger the compressor windings to ground (leads off) and each motor (condenser fan, blower) to ground; ohm each for shorts.
steps.expect: > 100 MΩ; no winding shorted.
steps.ifNot: < 1 MΩ or a dead short = the grounded component; replace it (compressor burnout: clean-up/driers).

steps.step: Inspect for shorted capacitors (bulged/leaking; a shorted cap reads ~0 Ω), chafed line-voltage wires against the cabinet, water in the disconnect/junction boxes, and burned terminals at the compressor and contactor.
steps.expect: No shorted caps or grounded wires.
steps.ifNot: Replace the cap / repair the wiring, seal the water entry.

steps.step: Delayed trips: clamp running amps on each leg vs nameplate RLA/FLA; compute voltage and current imbalance; compare the breaker/fuse size with the nameplate MOP and the wire size with MCA.
steps.expect: Amps ≤ RLA/FLA, imbalance ≤ 2 % V / 10 % A, protection sized ≤ MOP and ≥ MCA-based minimum.
steps.ifNot: High amps → head pressure/airflow/weak cap/low voltage; undersized or wrong-type protection → correct it (time-delay fuses for motor loads).

steps.step: Control fuse (3 A) blowing: see 'intermittent 24 V loss / control fuse blowing' — a shorted 24 V wire or coil.
steps.expect: 24 V circuit isolated and repaired.
steps.ifNot: Do not fit a larger fuse.

steps.step: After the repair: start the unit and monitor start amps (LRA spike duration) and running amps for 15+ minutes; verify the breaker/fuses stay cool.
steps.expect: Normal start, stable amps, cool protection.
steps.ifNot: Recheck for a second fault (e.g. compressor damaged by the short).

commonCauses: Grounded/shorted compressor winding or fan motor
Shorted run capacitor
Water in the disconnect or a chafed wire to the cabinet
Overload from high head pressure, low voltage, weak capacitor, or a seizing motor
Weak breaker or wrong fuse type/size
Loose connection heating the breaker/fuse clip

procedures.symptom: Compressor short cycles (runs briefly, stops, restarts repeatedly)
safety: Short cycling overheats start components and the compressor — do not leave a unit cycling on a safety while you diagnose elsewhere.
Momentary jumpers to identify the opener only; never leave a safety bypassed.

steps.step: Time the cycle and identify what ends the run: a board code (HPS/LPS/freeze), the overload (compressor stops, contactor stays in), the contactor dropping (24 V chain), or the thermostat/BAS call dropping.
steps.expect: The terminating device is identified.
steps.ifNot: Watch the contactor and the 24 V at Y1 and the coil at the moment it stops.

steps.step: If Y drops: thermostat location/anticipator/cycle rate, BAS staging or a stat wired to the wrong stage, a loose Y/R wire, or a fault (intermittent 24 V).
steps.expect: Y steady through the run.
steps.ifNot: Go to 'call present but unit idle' / 'intermittent 24 V loss'.

steps.step: If a pressure switch ends the run: gauges on. HPS → high head (dirty condenser, dead fan, fan cycling control, overcharge, non-condensables); LPS → low suction (low charge, restriction, low airflow, iced coil, low ambient without head-pressure control).
steps.expect: Pressure at trip matches the switch label; root cause on the refrigerant/airflow side.
steps.ifNot: Trip at a normal pressure → switch drifted → replace.

steps.step: If the compressor overload ends the run with the contactor still in: check amps vs RLA, voltage under load, voltage/current imbalance, run capacitor, condenser airflow, and the compressor's cooling (suction gas superheat too high = low charge).
steps.expect: Amps ≤ RLA, balanced supply, cap in tolerance.
steps.ifNot: Correct the overload cause; if the shell is very hot with normal amps, suspect internal problems.

steps.step: Check the anti-short-cycle protection (board, stat, timer) is in place and working: minimum off time 3–5 min.
steps.expect: The unit cannot restart within the delay.
steps.ifNot: A jumpered/failed timer lets the compressor slam back on against head pressure — restore the delay.

steps.step: Oversized unit / low load (space satisfies quickly): confirm with run times and delta-T; consider staging, fan cycling, or setpoint deadband changes rather than a repair.
steps.expect: Cycle length consistent with the load.
steps.ifNot: Document as an application issue.

commonCauses: High-pressure switch trips (dirty condenser, condenser fan failure)
Low-pressure switch trips (low charge, restriction, iced evaporator, low airflow)
Compressor overload from high amps / poor motor cooling
Thermostat/BAS call dropping (location, cycle rate, loose wire)
Anti-short-cycle timer bypassed or failed
Oversized equipment or low load

procedures.symptom: Condenser (outdoor) fan not running — compressor runs, head pressure climbs, HPS trips
safety: Fan blades can start without warning (fan cycling controls, delays) — lock out before reaching into the fan section.
Discharge the fan capacitor before handling; the motor shell may be hot enough to burn.
Shut the compressor down if head pressure is rising with the fan dead.

steps.step: With the compressor running and a fan call, read line voltage at the fan motor leads (after any fan cycling switch / head-pressure control / fan relay).
steps.expect: Line voltage at the motor.
steps.ifNot: No voltage: open fan cycling switch (check pressure vs setpoint), open fan relay/contactor pole, broken wire, or the board is holding the fan off (low ambient logic, defrost on heat pumps — normal during defrost).

steps.step: Voltage present, motor humming or dead: power off, spin the blade by hand.
steps.expect: Spins freely for several turns.
steps.ifNot: Seized/rough bearings → replace the motor (check the blade and rain shield too).

steps.step: Spins freely: test the FAN section of the capacitor (under load 2652 × A / V on the FAN lead, or bench).
steps.expect: Within ±6 % of rating.
steps.ifNot: Replace the capacitor (the exact µF the motor label calls for).

steps.step: Cap good, voltage present, spins freely, still no run: ohm the windings and check for a tripped internal thermal overload (motor hot → let it cool 20–30 min and retry).
steps.expect: Windings continuous; runs when cool.
steps.ifNot: Open winding cold, or grounded → replace the motor (match HP, RPM, volts, frame, shaft, rotation).

steps.step: Motor runs but slowly / wrong direction / high amps: verify rotation (air should blow up/out per the design), the blade pitch/diameter, and amps vs FLA; on speed-controlled fans verify the control's sensor and setpoint.
steps.expect: Correct rotation, amps ≤ FLA.
steps.ifNot: Reversed rotation on a reversible motor → change the rotation plug/leads; high amps → wrong blade or wrong motor.

steps.step: Verify head pressure returns to normal and clear any HPS lockout.
steps.expect: Condensing temperature ≈ ambient + 15–30 °F.
steps.ifNot: Continue with condenser cleaning / refrigerant-side diagnosis.

commonCauses: Seized fan motor bearings
Failed fan run capacitor (FAN section of the dual cap)
Fan cycling switch or head-pressure control open/failed
Motor thermal overload tripped (hot motor, high ambient, dirty motor)
Open fan relay/contactor pole or broken lead
Board holding the fan off (defrost, low-ambient logic)

procedures.symptom: Indoor blower (supply fan) won't run — belt-drive or PSC direct-drive
safety: Lock out and verify the wheel is stopped before entering the blower compartment; belt drives pull fingers in.
Electric heat or gas heat with no airflow trips limits — do not force a heat call while diagnosing the blower.
Discharge motor capacitors before handling.

steps.step: Confirm the fan call: G (or the board's fan output) = 24 V with a fan call; the board/relay energized (LED or click).
steps.expect: 24 V on G–C at the board; fan relay/contactor (IFC/IFR) energized.
steps.ifNot: No G: thermostat/BAS fan mode, stat wire; G present but no relay action → board fan output or relay coil.

steps.step: Read line voltage at the fan contactor/relay LOAD side and at the motor leads (all legs on 3-phase).
steps.expect: Full voltage at the motor terminals.
steps.ifNot: Burned relay contacts/contactor pole, open motor overload/starter (reset and check heater size), blown motor fuse, open door interlock, VFD not running (see the VFD procedure).

steps.step: Voltage present, motor not turning: power off, spin the motor/wheel by hand; check the belt (broken/slipped), sheaves and set screws.
steps.expect: Motor and wheel spin freely; belt intact and tensioned.
steps.ifNot: Seized bearings → motor/blower bearing replacement; broken belt → replace (then check why: alignment, tension, sheave wear).

steps.step: PSC direct-drive: test the run capacitor under load or bench; check the speed-tap connection.
steps.expect: Cap within ±6 %; correct tap energized.
steps.ifNot: Replace the cap / correct the tap.

steps.step: Ohm the windings (3-phase legs within 5 %; PSC common-run/common-start continuous) and megger to ground; consider a tripped internal thermal overload on a hot motor.
steps.expect: Windings good, > 100 MΩ.
steps.ifNot: Open/grounded → replace the motor (match HP, RPM, frame, volts, rotation).

steps.step: Motor runs: verify rotation, amps vs FLA (panels on), and airflow (static/temperature rise).
steps.expect: Amps ≤ FLA, airflow within design.
steps.ifNot: High amps → sheave too open / low static; low amps + poor airflow → reversed rotation or a wheel loose on the shaft.

commonCauses: Broken or slipped belt; seized blower or motor bearings
Fan relay/contactor contacts burned or coil open
Motor overload/starter tripped; blown fuse
Failed run capacitor (PSC)
Board fan output or G call missing
VFD faulted / not enabled

procedures.symptom: Indoor blower runs constantly / won't shut off
safety: On A2L (R-32/R-454B) units a blower running with no call may be RDS mitigation — check the board code BEFORE assuming a relay fault, and treat a leak alarm as real (ventilate, no ignition sources).
Lock out before pulling relays or touching line-voltage fan wiring.

steps.step: Check the thermostat/BAS fan mode (ON vs AUTO), occupancy schedule (occupied mode runs the fan continuously on most commercial RTUs), and any fan-on override.
steps.expect: Fan set to AUTO / unoccupied and still running.
steps.ifNot: Continuous fan in occupied mode is normal — explain, adjust the schedule if wanted.

steps.step: Read the board's fault code: RDS mitigation (A2L), a limit/rollout trip that runs the fan to cool the heat exchanger, a stuck-open limit, or a 'fan on for smoke detector/pressurization' input.
steps.expect: No fault; no mitigation active.
steps.ifNot: Diagnose the fault the board shows (A2L: 'a2l_mitigation_active'; limits: 'no heat on gas RTU').

steps.step: Read G–C at the unit terminal strip with the stat in AUTO and no call.
steps.expect: 0 V on G.
steps.ifNot: 24 V on G with no call = thermostat or a shorted G wire (G to R) — disconnect G at the strip: fan stops → stat/wire.

steps.step: G = 0 V and the fan still runs: check the fan relay/contactor (IFR/IFC) — welded contacts (fan runs with the coil de-energized) or a board fan relay stuck.
steps.expect: Relay contacts open with the coil de-energized; motor voltage 0 V.
steps.ifNot: Power off; if the relay contacts read closed with no coil voltage → replace the relay/board.

steps.step: Check the fan limit / fan-off delay: gas units run the fan for a post-purge (60–180 s) after heat; a limit switch stuck open keeps the fan on; a fan-limit control set to 'manual on'.
steps.expect: Fan stops after the normal off delay.
steps.ifNot: Replace the limit / set the control.

steps.step: ECM/constant torque motors: a tap continuously energized (backfed through another tap or a mis-wired humidifier/EAC relay) runs the motor with no call — check each tap for 24 V with no call.
steps.expect: 0 V on all taps with no call.
steps.ifNot: Find the backfeed (isolation relay needed for accessories).

commonCauses: Thermostat fan ON / occupied schedule (normal)
RDS mitigation active on A2L units
Welded fan relay/contactor contacts or a stuck board relay
Shorted G wire or a thermostat fault
Limit switch stuck open (fan runs to cool the heat exchanger)
ECM tap backfed by an accessory

procedures.symptom: Intermittent loss of 24 V control power / control fuse (3 A) keeps blowing
aliases: blows the fuse when it calls
safety: Never install a larger control fuse or a jumper across the fuse holder — the transformer will burn and the wiring can ignite.
Line voltage is next to the 24 V terminals in most panels; identify before probing.
Use a temporary 3 A automotive-style fuse or a fused jumper for isolation tests, and remove it when done.

steps.step: Determine when the fuse blows: at power-up (short present all the time) or only on a specific call (Y, G, W, O, economizer) — that call's circuit contains the short.
steps.expect: Pattern narrows the circuit.
steps.ifNot: If random: suspect a rubbing wire (roof curb, damper linkage, blower compartment) or moisture in a thermostat/sensor.

steps.step: Power off. Disconnect all thermostat wires at the unit strip and ohm each stat wire to C and to ground, and R to ground.
steps.expect: OL on every wire to ground and to C (except intentional C).
steps.ifNot: A wire shorted to ground/C = damaged stat cable (rodents, staples, curb chafe) — replace the cable or the damaged section.

steps.step: Isolate loads one at a time: remove one lead from each 24 V coil/accessory (contactor coil, fan relay, reversing valve solenoid, economizer actuator, damper actuator, humidifier, UV light transformer) and ohm each coil.
steps.expect: Coils read their normal resistance (contactor 10–30 Ω, relays 50–300 Ω); nothing reads ~0 Ω or to ground.
steps.ifNot: A shorted coil/actuator → replace it.

steps.step: Check the transformer sizing: add up the VA of everything on it (accessories added over the years) and clamp the secondary under the heaviest call.
steps.expect: Amps × 24 ≤ nameplate VA; ≥ 22 V at the board under load.
steps.ifNot: Overloaded transformer → add a separate transformer for accessories (with an isolation relay), do not upsize the fuse.

steps.step: Intermittent loss without a blown fuse: wiggle-test connections at the transformer secondary, the fuse holder (corroded/loose clips), the board's R/C terminals, and the door interlock switch; check for a thermostat cable splice in the return air.
steps.expect: Stable 24 V through the wiggle test and thermal cycling.
steps.ifNot: Re-terminate, replace the fuse holder, replace the door switch.

steps.step: Replace the fuse with the correct 3 A rating, restore all leads, and run every call (Y1, Y2, G, W1, W2, O/B, economizer) while watching the secondary current.
steps.expect: All calls work; secondary current within VA.
steps.ifNot: The last call that blows it contains the fault — isolate again within that circuit.

commonCauses: Thermostat cable shorted to ground/C (rodents, roof-curb chafe, staples)
Shorted 24 V coil (contactor, reversing valve solenoid, relay) or damper actuator
Overloaded control transformer from added accessories
Corroded fuse holder / loose secondary connections
Miswired thermostat (R to C) or a failed thermostat
Water in the economizer/sensor wiring

procedures.symptom: High-pressure switch trips / high head pressure lockout
safety: Never leave the HPS bypassed; a momentary, attended jumper with gauges on is only to prove the switch is the opener.
Discharge pressures can exceed 600 psig — use hoses/gauges rated for the refrigerant; stand clear of relief valves.
A2L units: HPS trips can accompany a leak/mitigation — check the RDS state before opening the system.

steps.step: Gauges on; confirm the head pressure at trip against the switch label (R-410A typically 600–650 psig; R-22 ~ 400–450; verify).
steps.expect: Trip pressure matches the label.
steps.ifNot: Trips well below the setting = switch drifted/oil-fouled capillary → replace; never adjust a factory switch.

steps.step: Check the condenser fan(s): running, correct rotation, full speed, fan cycling/head-pressure control not holding the fan off in warm weather.
steps.expect: All condenser fans running at full speed above ~ 65 °F ambient.
steps.ifNot: See 'condenser fan dead'; fix the fan cycling control setting.

steps.step: Inspect the condenser coil: dirt, cottonwood, grease, bent fins, recirculation (blocked discharge, adjacent unit exhaust), airflow direction.
steps.expect: Clean coil; condensing temperature ≈ ambient + 15–30 °F (10–20 °F on high-efficiency/microchannel).
steps.ifNot: Clean the coil (both sides of a slab coil; split coil sections apart on double coils).

steps.step: Check the charge and non-condensables: subcooling high with a high condensing temperature = overcharge; a condensing pressure that stays high with the unit off and equalized (standing pressure above the saturation pressure at ambient) = air/non-condensables.
steps.expect: Subcooling at target; standing pressure = saturation at ambient.
steps.ifNot: Recover the excess charge / recover, evacuate and weigh in the charge.

steps.step: Check for a high-side restriction after the HPS tap (rare) or a closed/partially closed discharge/liquid service valve, and hot-gas/reheat valves stuck.
steps.expect: Service valves fully open; no temperature drop across valves/driers.
steps.ifNot: Open the valve / replace the restricted component.

steps.step: Clear the board lockout (power cycle/thermostat) after the fix and monitor head pressure for 15+ minutes at full load.
steps.expect: Head pressure stable within the normal range; no repeat trip.
steps.ifNot: Re-examine for intermittent fan problems (thermal overload cycling) or a failing fan speed control.

commonCauses: Dirty or blocked condenser coil
Condenser fan not running / wrong rotation / fan cycling control fault
Overcharge or non-condensables
Head-pressure control (fan speed) holding the fan slow in warm weather
Drifted HPS or oil-fouled sensing capillary
Closed service valve or high-side restriction

procedures.symptom: Low-pressure switch trips / low-pressure or loss-of-charge lockout
safety: Never jumper the LPS to get cooling; running a low-charge compressor overheats it and pumps out the oil.
A2L refrigerants: an LPS/loss-of-charge trip may mean a leak — check the RDS/mitigation status, ventilate, no ignition sources, A2L-rated equipment.
Momentary, attended diagnostic jumpers only, gauges on, removed before leaving.

steps.step: Read the board code and count: single LPS trip vs lockout after several; note the bypass timer (boards ignore LPS for the first 90–180 s and in defrost).
steps.expect: Code confirms LPS/LOC.
steps.ifNot: If the code is for the loss-of-charge switch, expect a near-empty system.

steps.step: Gauges on before the start: standing pressure. Then start (bypass the lockout by cycling power only) and watch suction pressure vs the switch label (R-410A LPS typically opens ~ 20–50 psig; LOC ~ 7 psig; verify).
steps.expect: Suction stays above the cut-out under load.
steps.ifNot: Trips at the label pressure → refrigerant-side cause; trips above it → switch.

steps.step: Check indoor airflow first: filters, evaporator coil (iced? dirty?), blower running at the right speed, belt, closed dampers/VAV boxes, economizer stuck open in cold weather.
steps.expect: Airflow at design (≈ 400 CFM/ton), coil clean, no ice.
steps.ifNot: Restore airflow; let the coil thaw fully before charge diagnosis.

steps.step: Check the charge: superheat/subcooling (TXV: subcooling low + superheat high = undercharge; fixed orifice: superheat high) and look for the leak (electronic detector, bubbles at joints, oil spots at the coil, Schraders, service valve caps).
steps.expect: Charge on target.
steps.ifNot: Find and repair the leak, evacuate to < 500 microns, weigh in the nameplate charge.

steps.step: Check for a restriction: temperature drop across the filter-drier (> 3 °F), frost at the TXV/orifice, a TXV that will not open (lost bulb charge, bulb loose), low condensing pressure starving the TXV in cold weather.
steps.expect: No drop across the drier; TXV controls superheat.
steps.ifNot: Replace the drier/TXV; add or repair head-pressure control for low-ambient operation.

steps.step: Low ambient: if the unit is cooling below ~ 55 °F outdoor (server rooms, economizer failure), verify the head-pressure control and the low-ambient kit are working.
steps.expect: Condensing pressure held high enough for the metering device.
steps.ifNot: Repair the fan cycling switch / speed control / flooding valve; fix the economizer so mechanical cooling is not needed at low ambient.

commonCauses: Low charge / refrigerant leak
Low indoor airflow (filters, iced or dirty coil, blower, dampers)
Liquid-line restriction (drier, TXV, kinked line)
Low ambient operation without working head-pressure control
TXV failed closed / lost bulb charge
Drifted LPS or a loss-of-charge switch on a near-empty system

procedures.symptom: No heat on a gas-fired RTU / furnace — ignition sequence troubleshooting
safety: NEVER bypass the rollout switch, high limit, auxiliary limit, or inducer pressure switch, and never jumper the gas valve — the sequence proves safe combustion conditions in order.
Smell gas or find a valve leaking through: shut the gas cock, ventilate, no ignition sources, leak-test before continuing.

After any burner, ignition, or heat-exchanger work: run a combustion analysis and test CO in the supply air and flue before returning the unit to service; inspect the heat exchanger for cracks when a rollout has tripped.
Lockouts clear by cycling the thermostat/power only after the cause is corrected.

steps.step: Read the ignition control's LED/diagnostic code and the thermostat/BAS heat call: W1 (and W2) to C = 24 V at the board with the stat calling.
steps.expect: 24 V on W1; board code shows where the sequence stops.
steps.ifNot: No W: thermostat/BAS mode/setpoint/schedule, stat wire; go to 'call present but unit idle'.

steps.step: Verify the safety string: read across the rollout switch(es), high limit, auxiliary limit — 24 V across a switch = open.
steps.expect: ~0 V across each; all closed cold.
steps.ifNot: Open rollout: inspect the heat exchanger, flue, burners, and gas pressure BEFORE resetting (manual reset). Open limit cold: replace with the exact rating; open limit hot: airflow/temperature rise problem.

steps.step: Inducer: does it run on the call? Measure line voltage at the inducer; then the pressure switch — inducer suction on a manometer vs the switch label (e.g. −0.6 in. w.c.); read across the switch contacts.
steps.expect: Inducer runs; suction exceeds the switch setting; switch closes (~0 V across).
steps.ifNot: No inducer: board output/motor. Switch not closing: blocked flue/inlet/condensate trap, cracked/plugged hose, weak inducer wheel, wrong switch for altitude; switch stuck closed before the inducer runs = board waits/locks out → replace the switch.

steps.step: Ignition: HSI should glow (measure ~120 V at the igniter, or the igniter current) for the warm-up period; spark systems should spark at the electrode. Then the gas valve receives 24 V.
steps.expect: Igniter glows/sparks; 24 V across the gas valve terminals at the end of the warm-up.
steps.ifNot: No glow with voltage: open/cracked igniter (ohm it cold). No voltage to the igniter/valve with safeties closed: board relay → replace the control.

steps.step: Gas valve energized, no flame: inlet gas pressure (natural ≈ 7 in. w.c. inlet, 3.5 in. w.c. manifold; LP ≈ 11 / 10 in. w.c. — verify nameplate), gas cock open, valve opening (listen/feel; pressure at the manifold port), plugged burners/orifices, igniter position relative to the burner.
steps.expect: Manifold pressure at nameplate with burners lit.
steps.ifNot: Correct the gas supply; replace a valve that has 24 V but no flow (do not disassemble valves).

steps.step: Burners light then drop out (flame failure retries → lockout): measure flame-sense current in series with the flame rod (DC µA). Minimums are board-specific — read the board label/IOM: Honeywell S86xx/S89xx/SmartValve ≈ 1.0 µA min (2–6 healthy); White-Rodgers 50A55/50E47 ≈ 0.7 µA min; most OEM RTU/furnace boards (Carrier IGC, Lennox SureLight, Trane) are satisfied at 0.5–1.5 µA with 2–6 µA typical.
steps.expect: Steady flame current with margin above the minimum.
steps.ifNot: Clean the rod (fine abrasive pad), check its position in the flame, the ceramic insulator, burner ground strap, board ground, and 120 V polarity/neutral; a cracked insulator or open lead reads 0 µA.

steps.step: Flame stable: verify the temperature rise against the nameplate (25–55 / 35–65 °F typical), the blower on/off delays, and that limits do not cycle; run the combustion analysis (O2/CO/CO air-free) and check CO in the supply air.
steps.expect: Rise within range; CO air-free within the manufacturer's limits (typically < 100 ppm; ambient supply CO 0 ppm).
steps.ifNot: High rise → airflow; high CO → burner/heat exchanger/venting problem — do not leave the unit in service.

commonCauses: Dirty/mispositioned flame sensor (ignites, drops out, locks out)
Pressure switch not proving (blocked flue, condensate trap, hose, weak inducer)
Failed hot-surface igniter
Rollout or limit open (heat exchanger, airflow, over-firing)
Gas supply: cock closed, low pressure, valve not opening
Ignition control board relay failure; no W call from the stat/BAS

procedures.symptom: Economizer not modulating — damper stuck open, stuck closed, or not economizing
safety: Release the actuator (button/lever) before moving the damper by hand; gears and linkage can pinch.
Roof edges and open hood sections — fall protection; secure the hood against wind.
Actuator 24 V shares the control transformer — a shorted actuator blows the control fuse.

steps.step: Read the controller's status: JADE/W7220 display (faults: MA/OA sensor fail, actuator fault, changeover values), W7212 LEDs, or the BAS economizer points.
steps.expect: No sensor/actuator faults; readings plausible for the day.
steps.ifNot: Replace the faulted sensor/actuator per the fault list (JADE sensors are the 20 kΩ Sylk types — verify).

steps.step: Verify the controller inputs: 24 VAC power, fan proving/occupied input, Y1 call, OAT/MAT/RAT sensor values vs a thermometer, enthalpy sensor 4–20 mA if fitted; minimum-position setting.
steps.expect: Sensors within ±2 °F of measured; inputs present.
steps.ifNot: Open/drifted sensor → replace and reposition (MAT sensor in the mixed-air stream after the damper, not in the sun/return only).

steps.step: Command the actuator: read the controller's 2–10 VDC output (or use the test/override mode) while watching the damper.
steps.expect: Voltage rises toward 10 V on a free-cooling call and the damper follows; falls to the minimum (~ 3–4 V) when not economizing; 2 V / closed when the fan is off.
steps.ifNot: Output present, no motion → actuator or linkage; no output with valid inputs → controller/changeover setting.

steps.step: Mechanical: release the actuator and stroke the damper by hand; check shaft clamps, linkage, blade bearings, hood ice/debris, and that the blades seal closed.
steps.expect: Smooth full travel; no binding.
steps.ifNot: Free the linkage, tighten clamps, replace seized bearings.

steps.step: Changeover logic: confirm the setpoint type (dry-bulb A/B/C/D dial, differential, enthalpy) is right for the climate and the day's conditions actually permit free cooling.
steps.expect: Economizing when outdoor conditions are below the changeover; mechanical cooling added when the mixed air cannot meet setpoint.
steps.ifNot: Adjust the setting; a dial at 'D' (~ 50 °F) rarely economizes; enthalpy sensors drift with age (replace every few years).

steps.step: Verify the consequences: damper stuck open in hot/cold weather → high cooling/heating load, coil freeze, HPS/LPS trips; stuck closed → ventilation/CO2 complaints. Confirm the minimum position with a CO2 or airflow check if IAQ is the complaint.
steps.expect: Damper closes to minimum with the fan on, fully closed with the fan off.
steps.ifNot: Document the setting change and the fault history for the BAS.

commonCauses: Failed or drifted mixed-air/outdoor-air/enthalpy sensor
Actuator failed or linkage/shaft clamp loose; damper blades seized
Controller changeover setpoint wrong for the climate
Loss of 24 V to the actuator (transformer overload, fuse)
Controller fault/lockout (JADE alarm) or BAS override
Minimum position mis-set after a repair

procedures.symptom: VFD fault or motor won't ramp — supply fan / condenser fan / compressor drive
safety: Lethal DC-bus voltage remains after power off: wait the manual's discharge time, then measure the bus < 50 VDC before touching terminals (NFPA 70E).
Never megger the motor or leads with the drive connected — disconnect the motor leads at the drive output first.
Bypass mode runs the motor across the line with full-voltage starts; verify the bypass contactor is dead during work.
480/575 V: CAT III/IV meter, arc-rated PPE for live measurements.

steps.step: Record the active fault and the fault history/log before resetting (with the time stamps and the drive's own recorded values: current, bus volts, frequency, temperature at trip).
steps.expect: Fault identified (OC/OV/UV/OH/GF/external/communication).
steps.ifNot: No fault but not running → skip to the control checks (step 4).

steps.step: By fault — first checks: OC: motor/cable shorted (disconnect and megger), mechanical binding (belt/bearing), accel ramp too fast, wrong motor data. OV: decel too fast (overhauling load), high line voltage. UV: line sag, loose input lug, blown input fuse, aged bus capacitors. OH: clogged heatsink/fan, high enclosure temperature, blocked louvers. GF: motor/cable insulation → megger with the drive disconnected.
steps.expect: First-check condition found and corrected.
steps.ifNot: Clear the fault after the fix; if it recurs with no external cause, suspect the drive (IGBT/bus caps).

steps.step: Input power: measure all three line-to-line voltages at the drive input and compute imbalance; check the input fuses and lug torque.
steps.expect: Balanced within 2 %, at nominal; fuses good.
steps.ifNot: Imbalance/sag → correct the supply; drives trip on ripple from imbalance.

steps.step: Control: HOA in AUTO (or HAND to test), run-enable/safety interlock input closed (freeze stat, smoke detector, high static switch, fire alarm relay are often in the enable circuit), speed reference present at the terminals (0–10 V / 4–20 mA / network) and the control-source parameter matches.
steps.expect: Enable present, reference tracks the BAS/board command, drive shows 'run'.
steps.ifNot: No enable/reference → the interlock or controller, not the drive; in HAND the motor runs → the auto command chain is the problem.

steps.step: Output: clamp all three output legs (do NOT trust the meter's output volts); compare with the keypad's current and frequency; check the motor for binding and the belt/sheaves.
steps.expect: Balanced output currents ≤ motor FLA; frequency ramps to command.
steps.ifNot: Missing/unbalanced leg → output stage, cable, or motor; motor FLA parameter wrong → set from the nameplate.

steps.step: Static-pressure control (supply fans): verify the duct static transducer reading vs a manometer, the setpoint, and the PID direction; a failed transducer drives the fan to max or min.
steps.expect: Fan speed modulates to hold static; transducer within ±0.1 in. w.c.
steps.ifNot: Replace the transducer / correct the tubing (kinked, disconnected).

steps.step: Return to AUTO, verify the drive's parameters are documented (save/backup), and monitor for repeat faults; check the drive's cooling fan and the enclosure filters.
steps.expect: Stable operation in AUTO.
steps.ifNot: Recurring faults with all external causes ruled out → drive replacement; match kW/HP, voltage, enclosure and control I/O.

commonCauses: Run enable/safety interlock open (freeze stat, smoke detector, high static) or HOA in OFF
Missing speed reference / failed static pressure transducer
Input voltage sag or imbalance; blown input fuse
Clogged heatsink / cooling fan (OH)
Motor or cable insulation failure (GF/OC) — megger with the drive disconnected
Accel/decel ramps or motor parameters set wrong; aged DC-bus capacitors

procedures.symptom: Phase loss / single-phasing — 3-phase unit loud hum, motors trip, phase monitor fault
safety: Shut the compressor and motors down immediately on a suspected single-phase condition — motors overheat within minutes on two legs.
480/575 V live measurements: CAT III/IV meter, arc-rated PPE (NFPA 70E). Prove the meter live-dead-live.
Lock out before replacing fuses/contactors; a single leg can remain live with the others dead.

steps.step: Stop the equipment. Read all three line-to-line voltages at the unit disconnect LINE side, then the load side, then the contactor line side.
steps.expect: All three pairs at nominal within 2 %.
steps.ifNot: A pair reading low/zero at the line side = utility/building panel (open fuse, breaker pole, lug); at the load side only = blown disconnect fuse or burned pole.

steps.step: Note the trap: with a motor connected, a lost leg can still read a 'ghost' voltage (regenerated through the motor windings). Read with the loads OFF (contactors open) to see the true leg; a leg that reads 30–60 % of nominal under load and normal unloaded is high-resistance, not open.
steps.expect: Consistent readings loaded vs unloaded.
steps.ifNot: High-resistance connection → locate with a voltage-drop across each connection under load and repair.

steps.step: Check every fuse individually (voltage across each under load), the disconnect blades/clips (heat discoloration), lugs (torque), and each contactor pole drop.
steps.expect: ~0 V across each fuse/pole; no discoloration.
steps.ifNot: Replace the blown fuse (same class/size) and find why it blew (a shorted motor/compressor often blows one leg); replace burned contactors/disconnects.

steps.step: Check the phase monitor: LED/fault type (loss, reversal, unbalance, under/over voltage) and its setpoint dial; verify it re-closes with the supply corrected.
steps.expect: OK indication; contact closed.
steps.ifNot: If the supply is proven good and balanced and the monitor still faults → replace the monitor; never jumper it.

steps.step: After correcting: verify phase sequence with a rotation meter (utility repairs and disconnect swaps change it) — scrolls must rotate correctly; check compressor amps/pressures on the first start.
steps.expect: Correct rotation; balanced currents ≤ 10 % imbalance.
steps.ifNot: Reversed → swap two incoming lines at the unit's line side (all motors) — see 'reversed rotation after power work'.

steps.step: Assess motor damage: megger the compressor and motors, check for a hot shell / burned smell, and check the oil for acid on a compressor that ran single-phased for long.
steps.expect: > 100 MΩ, windings balanced.
steps.ifNot: Low megohm or an unbalanced winding → replace before it fails on the next start.

commonCauses: Utility phase loss or a blown fuse upstream (panel, disconnect)
Burned contactor pole or disconnect blade
Loose/corroded lug creating a high-resistance leg
A shorted motor blowing one fuse
Phase monitor nuisance setting or failure
Reversed sequence after utility or electrical work

procedures.symptom: Reversed rotation after power work — scroll compressor loud, not pumping, fans backwards
safety: Stop a reversed scroll immediately — it overheats and can be damaged in minutes (Copeland AE4-1294).
Lock out before swapping leads; verify all legs dead; work at the unit's line side, not at a motor, unless only one motor is reversed.
Re-verify sequence with a rotation meter after any change; never rely on the sound alone.

steps.step: Confirm the symptom: scroll loud/rattling, suction and discharge pressures nearly equal, amps well below RLA, compressor warming fast; fans moving little air with high noise; blower amps low.
steps.expect: Signs match reverse rotation.
steps.ifNot: If pressures separate normally and amps are normal, rotation is correct — look elsewhere (IPR, valves).

steps.step: Check the history: utility transformer/service work, a replaced disconnect, contactor, VFD bypass, or a motor swap since the unit last ran correctly.
steps.expect: A power-side change explains the reversal.
steps.ifNot: No change and reversal detected → a phase monitor may be reporting a supply sequence change from the utility.

steps.step: Verify with a phase-rotation meter at the unit's line terminals (and compare with the phase monitor's indication).
steps.expect: Sequence matches the unit's required rotation (marked on the unit/phase monitor).
steps.ifNot: Reverse: lock out and swap any two incoming line leads at the disconnect load side or the unit terminal block — every motor in the unit reverses together.

steps.step: If only ONE motor is reversed (after that motor was replaced or its leads were disturbed), swap two leads at that motor only.
steps.expect: That motor's rotation corrected; others unchanged.
steps.ifNot: Reversible single-phase motors: change the rotation plug/lead per the motor label.

steps.step: Restart and confirm: scroll pumps (suction drops, discharge rises), amps near RLA, quiet; fan airflow direction correct; blower amps and static normal.
steps.expect: Normal operation.
steps.ifNot: If the scroll now pumps but is noisy/hot with high amps, it may have been damaged by extended reverse running — monitor and check the oil.

steps.step: Document the sequence and label the disconnect; check the phase monitor's reversal setting is enabled so it catches a future utility change.
steps.expect: Phase monitor enforces sequence.
steps.ifNot: Install a phase monitor on scroll units that lack one.

commonCauses: Utility/service transformer replacement changing the sequence
Disconnect, contactor, or VFD bypass rewired with two leads swapped
Motor replacement with leads swapped
Phase monitor removed or set to ignore reversal
Reversible motor rotation plug set wrong

procedures.symptom: ECM / X13 / constant-torque blower dead or won't run
safety: Line voltage is present at the ECM at all times; never unplug the motor's power connector under power (module damage and arc). Wait several minutes after power-off before unplugging the module.
Lock out before spinning the wheel or removing the motor.
Never energize two 24 V taps at once on X13/constant-torque motors.

steps.step: Test order 1 — HIGH VOLTAGE: with the unit powered (no call needed), read line voltage at the motor's power connector (L–N or L1–L2; 3-phase where applicable).
steps.expect: Nominal line voltage present continuously.
steps.ifNot: Door interlock, blown fuse, unplugged/burned connector, board line-voltage relay — repair the supply.

steps.step: Test order 2 — LOW-VOLTAGE COMMAND: X13/constant torque — 24 VAC between the energized tap (1–5) and C with a fan call; variable-speed — the control signal (serial/PWM/0–10 V per the board) plus 24 V common.
steps.expect: 24 V on exactly one tap (X13) or the correct data/PWM signal with the call.
steps.ifNot: Board fan output / tap wiring / thermostat G — the motor is fine; fix the command.

steps.step: Both present, motor dead: power off, lock out, spin the wheel by hand; check for obstructions, a loose wheel, water/ice.
steps.expect: Spins freely and quietly.
steps.ifNot: Seized bearings → motor (module may be reusable on separable designs).

steps.step: Separable module (ECM 2.3/3.0 style): power off, wait, unplug the module; ohm the three motor phase leads at the motor connector — equal within ±10 %, none to the shell; check the module's connector for corrosion/water.
steps.expect: Balanced windings, nothing to ground → motor good; dead module.
steps.ifNot: Unbalanced/open/grounded → replace the motor (and check the module).

steps.step: Motor twitches/rocks and stops, or runs then shuts down: high static (filters, coil, closed dampers), a module failing under load, or a rotor position sensing fault — measure static and check the module's connector.
steps.expect: Static within design; smooth ramp.
steps.ifNot: Reduce static; if the fault persists at normal static → replace the module/motor.

steps.step: Replacement: match the OEM part or a programmed universal (constant-torque motors need the correct tap/torque programming; variable-speed OEM motors are programmed per model); after install verify amps, airflow and that only one tap is energized per call.
steps.expect: Motor runs on every call at the expected airflow.
steps.ifNot: Re-check the tap mapping on the board and any accessory relays backfeeding taps.

commonCauses: Missing line voltage to the motor (door switch, fuse, connector)
No 24 V/data command (board fan output, tap wiring, thermostat G)
Failed ECM module (moisture, heat, voltage spikes)
Seized bearings / obstructed wheel
High static causing over-current shutdowns
Wrong programming on a replacement motor

procedures.symptom: Call present at the thermostat/BAS but the unit stays idle — verify the demand is reaching the unit
safety: Momentary diagnostic jumper only (R to Y1/G/W1 at the unit strip), attended, removed before leaving — it bypasses the thermostat's staging/delays, not the unit's safeties.
Do not jumper on communicating (data-bus) systems; use the board/thermostat diagnostics instead.
Line-voltage terminals are adjacent to the low-voltage strip in many panels.

steps.step: At the unit's low-voltage terminal strip/board, read R–C.
steps.ifNot: No R–C: transformer/control fuse/door switch → 'unit completely dead'.

steps.step: With the thermostat/BAS commanding cooling (or heat/fan), read each call terminal to C at the unit: Y1, Y2, W1, W2, G, O/B.
steps.expect: 24 VAC on every terminal the stat/BAS should be energizing (Y1 + G for stage-1 cooling; W1 for heat; O/B per heat-pump logic).
steps.ifNot: Missing call at the unit = the stat/BAS output or the wire. Missing G only = fan control setting; Y present without G on a commercial unit = normal if the board runs the fan on Y.

steps.step: If the call is missing: at the thermostat/DDC controller, check mode (COOL/HEAT/AUTO), setpoint vs space temperature, schedule/unoccupied setback, hold/override state, compressor lockout or minimum-off timers, outdoor-air lockouts (economizer-only or heat-pump balance points), and any alarm the controller is holding.
steps.expect: Controller intends to call and its output terminal shows 24 V.
steps.ifNot: Controller not calling by design (schedule/override/lockout) → adjust or explain; see 'BAS or thermostat override'.

steps.step: Controller output is 24 V but the unit terminal is 0 V: the wire. Ohm the conductor end-to-end (disconnect both ends) and to the others; look for splices, rodent damage, roof-curb chafe, or a relay/isolation module between the BAS and the unit (check its coil and contact).
steps.expect: Continuity, no shorts.
steps.ifNot: Repair/replace the cable or the interface relay.

steps.step: If the call IS present at the unit and it still does nothing: momentarily jumper R to Y1 (or G/W1) at the unit strip to remove the stat from the picture.
steps.expect: Unit responds identically to the jumper → the fault is in the unit (board delays, safety chain, contactor) — go to the matching procedure.
steps.ifNot: Unit runs on the jumper but not on the stat = weak/intermittent call (voltage drop, loose terminal, a stat output relay with high resistance) — read the call voltage under load (> 20 V).

steps.step: Check the board's own reasons for ignoring a call: anti-short-cycle/minimum-off timers, lockouts from prior faults (needs a reset), RDS mitigation (A2L), a jumper/DIP setting (e.g. 'BAS mode' expecting a different input), or an unoccupied input pulling the unit to setback.
steps.expect: Board LED/display shows the call accepted and the sequence starting.
steps.ifNot: Reset the lockout after correcting its cause; fix the configuration.

commonCauses: Thermostat/BAS not actually calling (schedule, override, mode, setpoint, lockout timers)
Open or damaged thermostat cable / interface relay between BAS and unit
Board lockout or delay from a previous fault
Communicating thermostat waiting on delays or in a fault state
Missing C reference causing a weak call (power-stealing stat)
Unit configuration (DIP/jumper/occupancy input) ignoring the call

procedures.symptom: Trace the 24 V safety chain to find the open device (cooling or heating call not reaching the contactor/board output)
safety: Diagnostic jumper rule: a jumper across a suspected open switch is momentary, attended, applied only to confirm the opener, and NEVER left in place — a bypassed safety runs the unit into damage or a fire.
Never jumper gas-heat safeties (rollout, limit, pressure switch), the RDS on A2L units, or a phase monitor.
Board inputs may be 24 VDC or resistive (thermistor) rather than switched 24 VAC — read the diagram before jumpering anything.

steps.step: Get the unit's ladder diagram (inside the control panel door) and identify the chain for the call in question. Typical cooling chain: TRAN → control fuse → board R → thermostat Y → HPS → LPS/LOC → freeze stat → condensate overflow switch → duct smoke detector(s) → fire-alarm shutdown relay → phase monitor contact → anti-short-cycle timer → contactor coil → C.
steps.expect: Every device in the chain identified with its designator and location.
steps.ifNot: Without a diagram, follow the wire from the contactor coil backwards physically.

steps.step: Read the board's diagnostic code first — modern boards wire each safety to its own input and name the open one.
steps.expect: Code names the device (HPS, LPS, freeze, condensate, smoke).
steps.ifNot: No code or a legacy hard-wired chain → meter method.

steps.step: Meter method A (walk the chain): common lead on C; with the call active, move the hot lead from device to device downstream from R.
steps.expect: 24 V at every point up to the open device; 0 V immediately after it.
steps.ifNot: 24 V all the way to the contactor coil but no pull-in = the coil (or its return to C) — ohm the coil.

steps.step: Meter method B (across each device): read voltage ACROSS each switch/contact with the call active.
steps.expect: ~0 V across closed devices; 24 V across the one that is open.
steps.ifNot: Two devices open → 24 V splits/reads odd; walk the chain instead.

steps.step: Confirm the opener with gauges/thermometer/its own indicator, not with a jumper: HPS/LPS → pressures vs setpoints; freeze stat → coil temperature; condensate switch → pan level/float; duct smoke → its LED/reset; fire relay → alarm panel state; phase monitor → its LED; timer → wait it out.
steps.expect: The device is open for a real reason (or is failed).
steps.ifNot: Open with normal conditions → the device failed; replace with the exact rating.

steps.step: If a momentary jumper is used to confirm a suspected failed switch: gauges on, hand on the disconnect, seconds only, then remove it, replace the device, and re-verify the chain end-to-end.
steps.expect: Unit runs with the jumper only for as long as it takes to confirm; permanent repair made.
steps.ifNot: Runs normally with the jumper but trips again immediately without it → the condition is real (e.g. real high pressure) — fix the cause, not the switch.

steps.step: Voltage reads low (< 20 V) rather than zero: a high-resistance contact/splice in the chain — read the drop across each device under load, re-terminate.
steps.expect: Full 24 V at the coil.
steps.ifNot: Overloaded transformer (see 'intermittent 24 V loss').

commonCauses: High- or low-pressure switch open (real pressure problem or a drifted switch)
Condensate overflow switch open (plugged drain)
Duct smoke detector tripped or dirty; fire-alarm relay open
Freeze stat open (airflow/charge)
Phase monitor tripped; anti-short-cycle timer timing
Loose spade/terminal, corroded splice, contactor coil open

procedures.symptom: A2L unit (R-32 / R-454B) — blower running continuously, no compressor/heat, RDS or leak fault displayed
safety: Treat an RDS leak alarm as a real flammable-refrigerant leak until proven otherwise: ventilate the space and the unit, eliminate ignition sources (no brazing, smoking, non-A2L-rated tools/lights, arcing switches with panels open), and use A2L-rated leak detectors, recovery machines and vacuum pumps.
NEVER bypass, jumper, disconnect or disable the RDS sensor or the mitigation blower to 'get the unit running'; do not clear the alarm without finding the cause.
Do not connect gauges or open the refrigerant circuit until the RDS state has been checked and the area ventilated; A2L charge limits per room area apply to repairs.
Lock out before servicing the sensor; sensor mounting/orientation and the OEM part are mandatory.

steps.step: Read the fault code on the board/thermostat before touching anything: distinguish 'refrigerant detected' from 'sensor fault / communication lost' from 'sensor end-of-life'.
steps.expect: Code identifies the reason for mitigation.
steps.ifNot: Blower on with no code → not mitigation; go to 'blower runs constantly'.

steps.step: Refrigerant detected: ventilate; with an A2L-rated detector check the indoor coil, drain pan area, line-set connections, Schraders, TXV/distributor joints and the sensor location; check system pressures only after the area is ventilated.
steps.expect: Leak found (or the sensor cleared after ventilation with a documented transient cause such as solvent/cleaner fumes).
steps.ifNot: No leak found and the sensor keeps alarming → suspect a contaminated/failed sensor (replace with the OEM part) — but rule out a slow leak with a pressure/standing check first.

steps.step: Sensor fault / communication / end-of-life: check the sensor's supply and data at its connector against the diagram, connector seating and cable damage (common after coil/filter service); replace the sensor with the OEM part if powered but not responding or flagged end-of-life (sensors have a finite service life, typically 10–15 years).
steps.expect: Sensor communicating, status OK.
steps.ifNot: No supply → board/harness.

steps.step: Repair any leak per A2L practice: recover with A2L-rated equipment, nitrogen purge while brazing (no refrigerant present), evacuate, weigh in the nameplate charge (never exceed it); pressure/leak test before recharging.
steps.expect: Leak-free system at nameplate charge.
steps.ifNot: Do not return an A2L unit to service with a known leak.

steps.step: Clear mitigation per the IOM (many boards hold the blower ≥ 5 minutes after the sensor clears, then need a power cycle or thermostat reset) and verify: blower returns to normal control, compressor and heat are allowed, no fault redisplayed.
steps.expect: Normal operation on a cooling call; no RDS alarm.
steps.ifNot: Alarm returns → re-check the sensor and for a residual leak; verify the board firmware/sensor pairing.

steps.step: Verify that no field-added ignition sources exist near the coil (non-A2L-listed UV lights, humidifiers, electric heat kits) and document the event (code, concentration if displayed, sensor replaced, leak location) for the site.
steps.expect: Installation compliant; record complete.
steps.ifNot: Remove/replace non-listed accessories; advise the customer.

commonCauses: Real refrigerant leak at the indoor coil / line set
Sensor end-of-life or drift
Sensor cable disconnected or damaged during service
Transient contamination (cleaning chemicals, refrigerant from nearby recovery)
Non-OEM or mis-mounted replacement sensor
Board/sensor communication fault

procedures.symptom: BAS or thermostat override / schedule keeping the unit off or in the wrong mode
safety: Coordinate with the building operator before changing BAS points or schedules; releasing an override may start equipment unexpectedly (lock out any unit being worked on).
Do not leave a BAS point in manual/override to 'make it work' — document the change and the reason.
A jumper at the unit to test bypasses the BAS's safety logic (e.g. smoke/pressurization) — momentary and attended only.

steps.step: At the BAS front end / controller (or the thermostat), check the unit's occupancy mode, schedule, holiday/exception schedules, and the current effective setpoints (occupied vs unoccupied heating/cooling setpoints).
steps.expect: Occupied with a cooling/heating setpoint the space temperature is beyond.
steps.ifNot: Unoccupied/setback = the unit is idle by design; adjust the schedule or use a temporary occupancy override.

steps.step: Look for overridden points: occupancy, enable, fan command, compressor stages, damper position, heating/cooling lockouts, outdoor-air lockouts (mechanical cooling disabled below an OAT, heat disabled above one), and alarms (high static, smoke, low temperature) latched by the controller.
steps.expect: No manual overrides; no latched alarms.
steps.ifNot: Release the override (with the operator's agreement) or reset the alarm after fixing its cause.

steps.step: Compare the controller's output points with the physical terminals: BAS 'Y1 command = ON' should give 24 V on Y1–C at the unit (or a relay closing).
steps.expect: Command and physical output agree.
steps.ifNot: Controller output relay/triac failed, an interface relay between BAS and unit failed, or wiring — see 'call present but unit idle'.

steps.step: Thermostats: check hold/permanent hold, keypad lockout, mode (OFF/COOL/HEAT/AUTO with a deadband), fan mode, the compressor protection timer, and any 'system in lockout' display; power-cycle a stat that shows a communication fault to the unit.
steps.expect: Stat intends to call and displays the call (snowflake/flame icon).
steps.ifNot: Reconfigure the stat; replace if it will not call with correct settings and 24 V on R–C.

steps.step: Verify occupancy inputs at the unit (occupancy sensor, BAS unoccupied contact, door/night-setback switch) are in the state you expect; a stuck 'unoccupied' contact holds commercial RTUs in setback with the damper closed.
steps.expect: Occupancy input reads occupied.
steps.ifNot: Repair the sensor/contact; temporary override at the stat/BAS to keep the space comfortable meanwhile.

steps.step: Leave the system in AUTO with overrides released and document any schedule/setpoint change for the building operator.
steps.expect: Unit follows the schedule; no lingering manual points.
steps.ifNot: Escalate to the controls contractor for programming faults.

commonCauses: Unoccupied schedule / setback, holiday schedule
Point overridden in manual at the BAS or a latched alarm
Outdoor-air lockout of mechanical cooling/heating
Thermostat hold, mode, keypad lockout, or compressor protection timer
Failed BAS output relay or interface relay
Occupancy sensor/contact stuck unoccupied
